To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
physical interaction and activity within an environment are crucial for its effects on hippocampal neuroplasticity.
the beneficial effects of enriched environments on adult neurogenesis and learning and memory performance are mediated by physical interaction and direct exposure to the stimulus-rich environment.
direct experience of environmental enrichment is necessary to enhance hippocampal neuroplasticity and learning performance in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how much direct interaction with the outer world is required to enhance neuroplasticity and cognitive functions.
the question how the beneficial effects of enriched environments are induced.

the question of whether it is the direct interaction with a stimulus-rich environment that is responsible for the beneficial effects on adult neurogenesis and learning or whether mere exposure to the enriched environment is sufficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mere observation of a rich environment does not have the same effects on the brain as actively exploring the same environment.
direct experience of the environment is essential to induce structural and behavioral plasticity in the adult brain.
only direct interaction with the environment is sufficient to induce structural and cognitive changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mere representation of a stimulus-rich environment in television or in the form of virtual reality is insufficient to improve cognitive functions in mice.
direct interaction is necessary to induce beneficial effects in the brain and that indirect exposure is insufficient.
the effects of environmental enrichment depend on direct interaction of the animal with the stimulus rich environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
direct physical interaction with the environment is necessary to induce beneficial effects on hippocampal neuroplasticity and cognitive functions.
the beneficial effects of the enriched environment are dependent on direct interaction of the mouse with the enriched environment.
mere exposure to a stimulus-rich environment is not sufficient for the beneficial effects on neurogenesis and learning performance.
